title: Flying Leaves from East and West
short_title: Flying Leaves from East and West
publisher: Field and Tuer, the Leadenhall Press
summary: Emily Pfeiffer (1827–1890), a Welsh-born poet, describes two journeys. In the autumn and winter of 1882–83 she stayed with relatives near Smyrna (now İzmir, Turkey), visited the harem of the former governor Midhat Pasha and made an excursion to Magnesia, then went on to Athens, where she writes at length about Greek sculpture, Greek drama and Plato’s view of women.

In September 1884 she and her husband landed at New York and travelled by rail through Saratoga, Montreal, Ottawa, Toronto and Niagara to Chicago, a German farming settlement in Wisconsin where his relatives lived, Colorado, Salt Lake City, San Francisco and the Yosemite Valley, returning east by St. Louis, Washington and Boston. The Salt Lake City chapters report conversations with Mormon women about polygamy. The last chapters are reflections on American society, the position of women, and race. The chapters are called “Leaves”.
subjects: Travel in the United States and Canada
